title: Answer the API caller truthfully when the host is silent or out of reach

blocks.text: Your payment API answers each purchase with an HTTP status, and its callers act on it. A 503 makes the caller retry at once or offer another payment method. A 504 tells it to wait while a reversal job settles the purchase. Support has two complaints. On busy days some callers get a 500 with a `NullPointerException` in the log. And during last week's host restart, every caller waited the full timeout for a 504, and the reversal job then sent hundreds of reversals for purchases the host had never seen.
Finish the two places marked `TODO` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PaymentEndpoint.java`:

items: `statusOf(...)`: the status once the wait is over, and which purchases go on `unknown`.

blocks.text: The constants at the top of the class are the four statuses. About seven lines in total.
The tests run a real QMUX against a host on the far side of its queues. That host keeps reading `host-send` even while the QMUX reports the link as down, the way the adaptor would once it reconnects.

cases.says: a purchase the host approves is forwarded once and answered with 200
an answer whose field 39 is not 00 is a decline, so getting an answer at all does not mean approved
no answer in time comes back as null, which is an unknown outcome to record, not an error
a purchase with no answer is never sent a second time, because the host may already have approved it
with the link down the purchase is not handed to the MUX at all, since request() would queue it and send it later

origin.section: 4.4 A Request on a Down Link Waits in the Queue

concepts: request() does not check the link: on a down link the message waits in the queue for the timeout and may go out later, so the client asks isConnected() first and reports the host as unavailable.
request() returns null when no answer comes in time; that is an unknown outcome, not an exception, not a decline and not a reason to resend.
